title: Fix explainer page: glossary, card titles, claim order, tests
summary: Fix the firstmate explainer page, produced by xtask/src/site.rs from studies/firstmate-work-handling/*.json, so a first-time reader can follow it. Terms get defined or linked where 'Start here' first uses them, the Glossary is complete and sorted, cards get titles, the lede is clearer, claims are in numeric order with no repeated source, and generator tests guard this.

defaults_applied.how: New generator tests added; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
The criteria check the rendered page and sorted, deduplicated output, not just that the fields exist.
The ordering and dedupe rules are enforced in the generator and by tests, not only by fixing the one instance in the data.
Definitions and titles are written for an outside reader.
Verification runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused change to the page generator and its study data.
The generator and its tests are Rust.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: a newcomer reading the generated explainer page, and the maintainer reviewing the generator. The goal is a page that is readable without prior knowledge of firstmate.
The page is generated from studies/firstmate-work-handling/*.json by xtask/src/site.rs. Wording fixes go in the data and structural fixes in the generator.
Observed: claims.json lists c34 before c33. Duplicate sources are not yet deduplicated in the render loop, and I did not count how many claims repeat a source.

'home' is read as a firstmate home (a project's backlog or workspace, used by 'backlog item' and 'secondmate'). Green and red are read as the PR check status that yolo uses to decide whether to merge.
The best fix for claim order is to sort in the generator, so the page is robust even if the data is out of order. Fixing claims.json order as well is optional.
Decision: dedupe in the generator by (path, start, end) per claim, and fix any duplicated sources in the data only if the generator would otherwise hide them.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: In the rendered 'Start here' section, the first use of captain, yolo, green/red and local-only is either defined in place or links to its Glossary entry (the glossary dt ids are term-<name>). A reader can check this in the rendered HTML or in intro.json.
intro.json glossary has new entries for green, red and home, each with a definition. Entries that cite claims have valid claim ids, and page-only terms are marked about=page.
The Glossary renders in case-insensitive alphabetical order by term, whether the sort is done in the generator or the data is stored sorted. Any term added later is placed correctly.
Each rationale ra1–ra6 has a short descriptive title in rationales.json. The card heading renders that title and still shows the id, instead of the bare id alone.
The lede no longer shows the raw study_id unexplained. It either explains the id in plain words or leaves it out, and the pinned commit still appears.

In the rendered Claims and sources list, each claim lists a given source link only once. Claims appear in numeric id order (c33 before c34, the order that is currently swapped), and c10 comes after c9.

Run `cargo test -p xtask`. It passes and includes new tests that fail if the Glossary is unsorted, if a claim repeats a source, or if claims are out of numeric order. The tests run against the real study and against a small fixture that deliberately breaks each rule.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes. Existing site tests, including those that assert section order, still pass.

out_of_scope: Changing the study's claims, pin, findings or validation records beyond order or duplicate sources.
Redesigning the page layout or CSS.
Re-studying firstmate or changing the pinned commit.
Changes to governance files or lint configuration.
departures: No departure. The request has seven separate asks, which makes a verifier miss more likely, but the reference forecast already covers that.
